headline: South Korea Eases Margin Trading Rules to Prevent Forced Sales
summary: South Korea has eased its margin trading rules in an effort to stem forced stock liquidations.
why: Regulatory adjustments to margin requirements can reduce systemic liquidation pressure during market downturns and support investor liquidity.

impacts.name: South Korea
impacts.why: Regulatory easing aims to prevent cascading forced equity liquidations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Authorities relaxed margin rules specifically to prevent forced stock sales during periods of market stress.
